why: HOW A WORKFLOW CALLS ONE METHOD OF ONE ACTOR (ADR 0067). Today the Go handler's backing workflow (runtime/handler/workflow.go) makes these choices; after Phase 2 the CALLER does, in each SDK (sdk/python/kontra/catalog.py, sdk/go/catalog), with no sidecar in between. Every value here is one a drift turns into a quiet failure: a different actor_id lands a retry on a fresh instance that re-runs committed Units; a different queue is a batch nobody polls; a different heartbeat bound kills a legitimately slow Unit or leaves a wedged one alive for an hour. So the values are pinned FIRST, against the handler that has them today, and every caller that replaces it drives the same rows.
derived_by: runtime/handler/workflow.go (today's backing workflow; deleted when Phase 2 lands)

activities.why: The activity type names. RunBatch and Close are served by the actor process today; the blob pair is served by the orchestrator's dataset worker after Phase 2 (it already has the object store, in every namespace).

actor_id.why: Which live instance (and which commit map) a batch belongs to: the idempotency key, else the Session, else run and node joined with `-`, empty parts skipped. A retry derives the SAME id, which is what lands it on the instance holding the batch's progress.

cases.why: a keyed actor (a virtual object): the key wins over everything
an unscoped call: run and node
a node with no run id keeps only what is there

refused.why: nothing to key the instance by

run_options.why: RunBatch's activity options. StartToClose is generous because the heartbeat, not the clock, is what catches a wedge: the actor beats per committed Unit and on a keepalive. A dispatch may RELAX the heartbeat for a debugger (never tighten it), capped at StartToClose. A scoped call waits at most a minute for its Session's worker; an unscoped one waits for capacity with no bound.

heartbeat.why: a request below the default cannot tighten it

close_options.why: Close runs only for an UNSCOPED call — a Session's close is the scope's exit — on the same queue as the RunBatch, briefly and with few retries: a close that cannot run is a leak to report, not a reason to fail a batch that succeeded.

blob_options.why: fetch_blob and store_blob: bounded and short.

queue.why: Where RunBatch is scheduled: an unscoped call on the actor version's sessions queue (every worker of the version polls it), a scoped call on its Session's own queue. Names are queues.json's; this pins WHICH one a call uses.
